title: OTP Applications: .app.src, -behaviour(application) & Runtime Configuration
solutionExplanation: Implements both application and root supervisor behaviours, managing application start/stop lifecycles and runtime configuration parameters via application:get_env and set_env.

otpDocCards.description: Loads and starts an OTP application and all of its dependencies, spawning its application master and root supervisor.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Synchronous boot. Fails if dependencies are not already started.

otpDocCards.description: Fetches configuration parameter Par for Application. If undefined, returns Def.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Fast O(1) concurrent ETS read inside application controller.

mentalModelCheck.question: Who invokes the start/2 callback of an OTP application module?

options.label: The BEAM Application Master process, when the application is booted via application:start/1 or an OTP release.
options.explanation: The Application Master is an internal OTP process created to isolate and manage the lifecycle of each running application.

options.label: The developer manually from the terminal shell.
options.explanation: Developers call application:start(App); the Application Master invokes the callback Mod:start/2.

options.label: The Linux systemd service manager directly.
options.explanation: systemd starts the Erlang runtime node (erl/beam.smp); OTP manages its own internal application tree.

options.label: The first client that makes an HTTP request.
options.explanation: Applications boot deterministically on node startup, not lazily on request.
